S84.01.note: Whether every string translates is not judged here; the selector itself calls i18n.changeLanguage.
steps: Sign in and open the account menu, then click Settings.
On the General page, find the Preferences heading and the Display Language row.
Open the Display Language dropdown (it lists languages by their own names) and pick a different language.
Look at the page: the labels and menu text should switch to the chosen language, as Expected says.

S84.03.note: Persistence across reload is handled by the useAppTheme hook; the code was not run.
steps: Open Settings and click Appearance in the settings list.
Under Theme, click Light, then Dark, then System.
After each click, look at the whole page colours and check the chosen button is marked active.
Reload the page and check the same theme is still selected.

S84.04.note: The web app always shows the swatches; no per-plan gate was found in the row.
steps: Open Settings > Appearance.
Find the Accent colour row of colour circles.
Click one circle (each is labelled with its colour name followed by accent).
Look for the check mark on the chosen circle and for buttons, links and highlights to take that colour. Click another circle and compare.

S84.05.needs: a chat with at least one reply
S84.05.note: The size is applied through a data attribute on the root element (AppearancePreferences.tsx).
steps: Open Settings > Appearance.
Choose Large in the Chat text size dropdown.
Open a chat that has several replies.
Compare message text with Small and Default; the size should change across messages.

S84.07.note: The code offers System and Reduced only. Honouring the OS reduce-motion setting is not verified in code here; the OS-level CSS query was not searched.
steps: Open Settings > Appearance.
Under Motion, click Reduced.
Look at the interface and replies for less animation, for example while a reply streams or a menu opens.
Click System and compare the motion again.

S84.08.needs: a chat with a code block; dark mode to see the colours
S84.08.note: The theme list comes from CODE_THEMES; the individual theme names were not listed here.
steps: Open Settings > Appearance.
Choose a theme in the Code theme dropdown.
Open a chat that shows a code block, or ask for a short code sample.
Compare code colours; the hint says the colours apply in dark mode and light mode keeps high contrast.

S84.09.needs: a chat with a code block that has a long line
steps: Open Settings > Appearance.
Turn on the switch labelled Wrap long code lines.
Open a chat with a code block that has a very long line.
Check the long line wraps onto new lines; turn the switch off and check it no longer wraps.
S84.09.where: Settings > Appearance > Wrap long code lines

S84.10.needs: a Free account to see the Free choices; a paid account to pick a model marked Upgrade to use
S84.10.note: Models not on the plan show Upgrade to use and open a plan message instead of saving.
steps: Open Settings > General.
In Preferences, open the Default model dropdown.
Choose a model name, or leave Last used.
Start a new chat and check the model shown for it matches your choice.

S84.11.needs: a paid account to pick levels marked not on your plan
S84.11.note: The row hint says each chat can change the level in the composer.
steps: Open Settings > General.
In Preferences, open the Reasoning effort dropdown.
Choose a level other than Off.
Start a new chat and check the effort control in the composer shows that level.

S84.12.needs: none; if the hint under the row says your plan lacks Work, a plan that includes Work
S84.12.note: Expected mentions ask vs auto, but this row offers only Chat and Work. No ask or auto choice was found in General; the approval default sits under Capabilities as Default approval for tool actions.
steps: Open Settings > General.
In Preferences, open the New chats start in dropdown.
Choose Work, then click the new chat button and check the new chat opens in Work.
Set it back to Chat and check the next new chat opens in Chat.
S84.12.where: Settings > General > Preferences > New chats start in

S84.14.note: Expected says the user picks which modifier sends. The code offers no choice: the send keys are fixed to Cmd + Enter on Mac and Ctrl + Enter elsewhere.
steps: Open Settings > General and scroll to the Composer heading.
Turn Send with Enter on, go to a chat, type a line and press Enter; the message should send.
Read the hint under the switch: it names the send keys for this computer, such as Cmd + Enter on a Mac.
Turn the switch off, type a line and press Enter; it should start a new line, and the send keys should send.
S84.14.where: Settings > General > Composer > Send with Enter

S84.15.note: Only shortcuts the code marks rebindable get a Change keys button. Restore defaults asks for confirmation first.
steps: Open Settings and click Keyboard (or open General and click View shortcuts).
Find a shortcut with a Change keys for button and click it, then press a new key combination.
Turn that shortcut's switch off and check it is marked off in the list.
Click Restore defaults and confirm; check the keys and switches return to their defaults.
S84.15.where: Settings > Keyboard, or Settings > General > Preferences > Keyboard shortcuts > View shortcuts

S84.18.needs: none for Email; Browser needs browser notification permission; Mobile push needs the phone app (unsure)
S84.18.note: Channel names are Browser, Email and Mobile push. Whether each channel delivers is outside this code path and was not checked.
steps: Open Settings and click Notifications.
Find the row Scheduled task finished and open its dropdown.
Choose Email, then open it again and choose Off.
Check the row's selected value changes each time; the options list only channels released for this app.
S84.18.where: Settings > Notifications, then the dropdown on a row such as Scheduled task finished

S84.19.note: The switch has aria-label Enable quiet hours. The save control label was not located, and the switch is disabled while loading or saving. Holding of notifications is not checked here.
steps: Open Settings and click Time and focus.
Turn on the switch next to Quiet hours, then set Start, End and Days.
Click the save control on the page (its visible label was not found in code) and wait for the status text.
Reload the page and check Quiet hours still shows your times and days.
S84.19.where: Settings > Time and focus > Quiet hours

S84.23.note: Collapsed by default and auto-hide have no settings control. Searched apps/web/features/settings, apps/web/shared/stores/layout-store.ts (sidebarCollapsed, no setting) and packages/ui/ui/src/sidebar/Sidebar.tsx. Chat cannot be hidden.
steps: Open Settings > General and find the Sidebar items row.
Click a destination button to switch it off, then look at the left sidebar: that item should be gone.
Click the same button again to show it; the item returns.
Click the Toggle sidebar button in the sidebar and check it collapses; click again to expand.
S84.23.where: Settings > General > Preferences > Sidebar items (collapse: the Toggle sidebar button in the sidebar)
